Based on the retrieved matches, the covering of the resection margin after distal pancreatectomy is not shown to be an advantageous practice. The results indicate that there are no significant differences in fistula rates between those who cover their margins and those who do not. In fact, one study suggests that the covering of resection margins may even contribute to a "picture of an unsolved problem." Therefore, it appears that covering resection margins after distal pancreatectomy is not beneficial for patients or healthcare systems.

This recommendation comes from considering the provided information and evaluating the potential impact on patient outcomes.
